tool.name: discover_cloud_assets
tool.description:
Discover public cloud-storage assets (S3 / GCS / Azure Blob) by name permutation.
Generates candidate bucket names by combining the org name with a wordlist of common prefixes and suffixes (-prod, -staging, -uploads, -backups, etc.), then probes each candidate against AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage endpoints.
For each hit, emits a structured finding. A 200 response usually means public listing is exposed (`severity: medium`); a 403 typically means the bucket exists but listing is denied — still significant because it confirms the namespace is owned and may expose objects via direct-name reads (`severity: info`, recommended for follow-up).
Use this tool during the recon phase for any `domain` target — public cloud-storage exposure is one of the highest-value external-recon findings and is invisible to the agent's default reasoning loop.
Categories: `info_disclosure`. CWEs: `CWE-548` (exposed listing), `CWE-200` (info disclosure for owned-but-listing-denied buckets).

parameter.name: org_name
parameter.description: Organization or domain name. The leftmost DNS label is used as the bucket-name base. For "example.com" this is "example".

parameter.name: providers
parameter.description: Comma-separated subset of {s3, gcs, azure}. Default: "all". Restrict to a subset when the org's cloud provider is already known.

parameter.name: extra_suffixes
parameter.description: Comma-separated extra suffix wordlist to append to the default. Useful when the org has a known naming convention (e.g. "-customer-data,-tenant-uploads").

returns.description: {success, org_name, providers_checked, candidates_probed, hits: [...], hit_count}. Each hit has {provider, name, url, status, severity, reason, category, cwe}.
